explanation: Any W_out in Sym^2_0(R^3) can be connected to the degenerate set by a straight line (or short path). The degenerate set is a union of hyperplanes, so the nearest point is always at finite distance. The drift channel is universally available.
two_point_verdict: UNIVERSAL_REACHABILITY: The two-point Weyl connection problem is always solvable. The degenerate set in Sym^2_0(R^3) is a union of 3 hyperplanes (codimension 1), and any point can reach it by a bounded path. The exponential drift channel is not specific to special orbifold geometries.
